$comment: The president's deck. Assembled by content-assemble from batches president-1..5.

papers.text: Build Kitecombe a hill. The League currently launches from a chair.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: New string for the League. 61 % of the old string is in hedges.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A topiary kite on the kite field. Then its string, then its flyer.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Declare the Kitecombe maze kite-free. Kites inside may apply to leave.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A sign over the water, facing up: KITES, PLEASE GO ROUND.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: New shears for the Committee. The anglers' willow is worried.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: The League asks for a level playing field. The band's, ideally.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Roof the spotters' bench. Last year it logged 30 % kites.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Pose beside a hedge clipped in your likeness. A modest hedge.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Let the Guild arrange the hedges as a display. The Committee did them first.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: The Circle will pay for band practice indoors. Far indoors.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Awnings for the shop windows, printed: THIS IS NOT A LANDING.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: A net over the marrow beds. Last year a kite came second.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Judge the hedge show. All 212 are straight, so point at one and smile.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: An inquiry into why coaches come in threes. Three copies, in the Guild's window.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: Three more coaches came. The inquiry asks for three more windows.

papers.text: Ride the first coach of spring. You will be logged as luggage.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Hold the marrow show in the coach park. Parked coaches get weighed.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A committee to pick a tune, on the kite field. It will hear every tune first.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The tune committee heard every tune. Now it asks for an encore.

papers.text: The band would like a hearing. A sound shell by the water will do.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A sign on every hedge: KITES WELCOME. The hedges were not asked.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: The band will pay for a licence to echo. Anglers hear each tune twice.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Lend a shop window the founding napkin. The Guild will iron it.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: A study of silence by the water. So far: 70 % quiet, 30 % band.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The silence study needs a quieter room. It asks for the band's.

papers.text: The spotters will pay to stand in the marrow beds. Then to sit.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A working group to tie up loose ends: the kite strings in hedges.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The loose-ends group is stuck in a hedge. It asks for a rescue group.

papers.text: Be photographed waving from every coach. All of them, one a day.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Give the band's Sunday hour to the Circle. Same hour, fewer notes.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A hat for you. And one for your coach. And for each wheel, perhaps?
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: About the hat: it asks to be logged by the spotters as a coach.

clippings.sign: SPOTTERS TOLD TO LOG A HAT; HAT RUNS LATE
clippings.refuse: HAT IS NOT A COACH, PRESIDENT RULES

papers.text: The Guild will pay for a quiet day. Each tune rattles eleven panes.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Rodney has clipped your signature into a hedge. He proposes the rest.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Rename the riverbank BANDSTAND (TEMPORARY) on Thursdays. Fish informed.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Survey the hedges with kite string, pulled tight. The League lends it.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The string is not straight. The survey asks to survey the string.

papers.text: The growers will hire the kite field. Kites that land will be judged.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Lend the spotters a shop window. Coaches look better framed.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Pose with the prize marrow for its portrait. Slightly behind it.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: The League pays per kite fetched from hedges. The hedges hold 41.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A fruit basket, as before. A ribbon on it, as before. No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the basket: it would like a shop window. The Guild's best one.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S BASKET TAKES GUILD'S BEST WINDOW
clippings.refuse: BASKET REFUSED A WINDOW; TO BE EATEN INSTEAD

papers.text: A working group on what a marrow is. It meets on the kite field.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: Some marrows may be courgettes. The marrow group asks for a sub-group.

papers.text: A desk fountain, just for you. It tinkles. The next one up splashes.
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: About the fountain: it is lonely. It asks to live by the anglers' water.

clippings.sign: DESK FOUNTAIN MOVES TO RIVERBANK; ANGLERS HEAR TINKLING
clippings.refuse: FOUNTAIN STAYS ON DESK, TINKLING AT NOBODY

papers.text: The Committee will pay to trim the hedge spotters lean on. Leaning rescheduled.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A window in the hedge, for one hat. The hedge will hardly notice.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Give the band kite day. And the day after, for the encores.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: First prize at every show. Cuthbert has entered you as 'other'.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: We will pay to put the timetable in one shop window, the footnotes in six.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Call it the Hedge and Kite Show. Our kites are in it anyway.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: The band will hire a shop window. Display: ONE CORNET, IN USE.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Lend us the national bandstand for hats. The band may stay, as stands.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: An inquiry into 'mild' in kite forecasts. Onions want it defined.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The onions are content. They would now like 'fairly' looked into.

papers.text: Clip the kite field hedge into a clock. Accurate to the nearest season.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: An inquiry into why kites land on buses. It will sit on the top deck.
papers.subject: buses
papers.biggerStudy: The inquiry has outgrown the top deck. It asks for a second bus.

papers.text: Give the onion show the dry Saturday. Kites get the next, in spring.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Ladders for the hedges of Gusting Heights. 31 kites are waiting.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A desk fountain. It gurgles when you are right. It never stops.
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: Your desk fountain has entered the hedge show. It expects to win.

clippings.sign: FOUNTAIN WINS HEDGE SHOW; HEDGES DAMP AND DISMAYED
clippings.refuse: FOUNTAIN SENT BACK. IT HAS NOT GURGLED SINCE

papers.text: The band has our Thursdays by the lake. Now Fridays. One back, please.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Ribbon offcuts, to practise on. Any openings coming up? No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the offcuts: they want the best shop window. For a month.

clippings.sign: OFFCUTS TAKE BEST WINDOW; GUILD DISPLAYS ITS DISMAY
clippings.refuse: OFFCUTS RETURNED UNCUT. MR SASH 'NOT UPSET'

papers.text: We will pay to fly over the hedge show. Each kite has signed: I WILL NOT LAND.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A study of how far the band carries: from the lake, then the next lake.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The band study asks to listen from a third lake, to be thorough.

papers.text: We will sponsor the kite festival if kites keep in line. We drew the lines.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Sit with the anglers, for the front page. The band will whisper.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: The League would like to hire the wind over Brassby. They will pay.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Log a coach for the camera at the milliner's. It is already logged.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A kite festival working group. Item one: move the hedges.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The festival group must meet again. The hedges did not attend.

papers.text: A lid for the national bandstand. With a hole, for applause.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Wear our rosette to the kite festival. Onion morale is up 3 % already.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

papers.text: A barometer for your desk. It only ever says RAIN.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: About the barometer: it wants the 8:15 held until it has decided.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT HOLDS 8:15 FOR BAROMETER; SPOTTERS LOG DELAY
clippings.refuse: BAROMETER SENT BACK. IT SAW THIS COMING

papers.text: Move kite day away from the lake. Last year our floats took off.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Kites landed in the prize beds 12 times. One came second. A net, please.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: An inquiry into the shape of the wind. We would like it squarer.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The inquiry could not find the wind's corners. It asks to look again in autumn.

papers.text: Spotters lean on our hedge. Then flasks. Now a stepladder. Move the stop.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A ramp on Gusting Heights. The band is sitting on the good wind.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: An inquiry into nose prints on shop windows. Witnesses will be asked to lean.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The inquiry needs a second window. The first is evidence.

papers.text: Your speeches in gilt, beside the founding napkin. The napkin reads better.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Launch the season's first kite. Let go when we say. Not before.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A bandstand by the lake. The anglers have gone very quiet.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Every forecast to end with you. 'Light winds, then the President.'
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: An onion bed on the bandstand lawn. Dig the first hole, for the camera.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: Kites outnumber buses at the stop three to one. It is a bus stop.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A plaque on the draper's window: THE 8:15 WAS ON TIME HERE, ONCE.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Pose by our best window. It covers the bus timetable entirely.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will hire the 8:15 on show day. Onions only, one per seat.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: Dim the lighthouse so the fish can sleep. The band has torches.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: The hat show asks for the kite field. Hats fly too, briefly.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: Let us hire the arcade's glass roof. A bus is 12 % more bus from above.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: A practice hut by the anglers, labelled SOUNDPROOF (MOSTLY).
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Present the Quiet Competition cup. Applause will be by eyebrow.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A marquee for our show. Then over the bus stop. Then the bus.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: An inquiry: is a kite in the bay a fish? If so, nobody may pull it out.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The kite-or-fish inquiry wants a second summer. The kite is still in.

papers.text: Hold our spool for the camera. The kite is in the next province.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Your face on the new stamp. Mildred has seen three, and kept one.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: Register every hedge: name, age, and any kite it is holding.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: The parade, past our windows this year. The bus station has had nine.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Lend our prize onion the hat in the Guild's window. Then gloves.
papers.subject: hats

papers.text: We will pay to name the new holiday WINDOW DAY, not TIMETABLE DAY.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A study of ripples in Saltpenny Bay. So far, 40 % are the band's.
papers.subject: harbours
papers.biggerStudy: The ripple study would now like the waves. Ewan has a second pencil.

papers.text: A shop window on the pier. The sea has never been shown a hat.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Sit for the new coin: heads, you. Tails, a bus, not a shop bell.
papers.subject: portraits

papers.text: We will hire the Quiet Competition's interval. Then the rest of it.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: An inquiry into the kite on the Guild's awning. It will speak from there.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The awning inquiry asks for a second season. The kite has not answered.

papers.text: Give us the top deck's front seat. Kites fly 30 % higher from it.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Open the hedge show. The ribbon is a hedge; shears provided.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will hire the bandstand for the onion parade. Wave as they roll.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: The band asks for the harbour steps. Anglers may keep the wet ones.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Pin the first-prize rosette on the onion. Rodney has one for you.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A committee to date the new holiday. It meets only on holidays.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The holiday committee needs more holidays to meet on. Three, to start.

papers.text: Choose the band's encore at the bay. Same tune again, but yours.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A hat with a smaller hat on it. The smaller hat has a request.
papers.subject: hats

favour.text: The smaller hat asks for a place in the kite festival. It will need a string.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT FLIES HAT AT KITE FESTIVAL; KITES UNIMPRESSED
clippings.refuse: HAT REQUEST FILED FOR FURTHER STUDY

papers.text: We will hire the harbour for the holiday: 88 % quiet, 12 % goose.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A kite museum. The hedge outside holds most of the exhibits.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Hedge day and kite day clash. Ours was filed first, in triplicate.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A fanfare for each harbour ribbon. Scissors up on the last note.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A willow on the quay to sit under. The Committee may admire it.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A ceremony for your hundredth ceremony. First, a rehearsal ceremony.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: Be our window display for an hour. Your card: PRESIDENT, ONE ONLY.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A picnic chair, with an umbrella and a spare umbrella. No reason.
papers.subject: picnic-weather

favour.text: About the chair: it would like the front row at the show. Umbrella up.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT GIVES CHAIR FRONT ROW; GROWERS STAND
clippings.refuse: CHAIR SENT BACK; UMBRELLA STAYS UP, JUST IN CASE

papers.text: A study: do onions grow to brass? The band plays to them nightly.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The onion study wants a second bed, as a control. The band will play to both.

papers.text: A plaque for the harbour bus turn: IT TURNS HERE. See the shop door.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Clip the bus stop hedge into a bus. Then a queue. Then a late one.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Make your birthday a national holiday. Mildred has a drawer for these.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Hedge manners: a committee. Chapter one: may spotters lean? Two: no.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The manners committee wants a second volume: bowing to topiary.

papers.text: Move the harbour bus stop. Each horn undoes 40 minutes of quiet.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A motorway bench, where the hedge is, to watch coaches go by. They mostly do.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: An extra hour on show day, from the National Clock. Spotters can spare one.
papers.subject: clocks

papers.text: Lampshades for the street lamps. Then tassels. The bus stop's gets both.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Give us the League's telephone. We only ring for early coaches. Twice a year.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Tune one foghorn to the band. Then all of them. Then book a fog.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: We booked the bandstand on the band's form. Instrument: pumpkin.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: A bandstand on wheels, to go to the audience. It is at the kites.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Till's Teas will sponsor the motorway lamps, in tea colour. Milky.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Pose by our ten-thousandth coach. Lean on the hedge, as we do.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: An arcade sign: PRIZE PUMPKIN, THIS WAY. It points outside.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Lend us the spotters' footbridge. Coaches are a loyal audience: they keep coming.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Light the lay-by for night spotting. The marrows may not sleep.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: Kites get the harbour wall. Anglers may apply to sit on the water.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Cushion the harbour wall, for the echo. Then the bandstand. Then the band.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A kite that lands in a hedge now belongs to it. Form attached.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Hear the harbour band by telephone, for the camera. Nod.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: A lake lighthouse, for floats at dusk. It goes in the marrow bed.
papers.subject: inventions

papers.text: Lamp-post signs: KITES MAY REST HERE. In place of SHOPS THIS WAY.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Trim the arcade hedge. Then the awnings, to match. Then the hats.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Dim the Guild's harbour windows at dusk. The water is 40 % hat.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: The band will hire a lighthouse to play from. One bar per step, up to the top.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: Unhook the telephones for the Quiet Competition. Till's Teas is ringing.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: We will pay to keep the bandstand in trim. Shears are packed.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Walk the arcade with the band, carrying cymbals. Carrying only.
papers.subject: ceremonies

papers.text: A landing circle by the marrows. Kites miss circles by 3 metres.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: We will pay to put the pumpkin on the motorway signs. Coaches may follow it.
papers.subject: signage

papers.text: Launch a kite named after you. Smile before it finds the hedge.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: We will pay for dark harbour lamps at concerts. The band knows 30 % by heart.
papers.subject: harbours

papers.text: A study: is a coach late if nobody waits for it? The Guild is asked to wait.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The lateness study asks the Guild to wait at every stop, in turn.

papers.text: Your face on the National Clock. At noon both hands point at you.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A study of marrows by lamplight. Half the high street goes dark, as a control.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The marrow study now needs the lit half dark, and the dark half lit.

papers.text: A desk lamp. It glows near ribbons. Any openings soon? No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the lamp: it would like a solo at the Sunday concert.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S LAMP GIVEN SOLO; BAND PLAYS IN THE DARK
clippings.refuse: LAMP STAYS ON THE DESK, GLOWING AT NOTHING

papers.text: Light up the hedge show for the camera. Kites stay down until you smile.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: A study on the lighthouse window display. Shortlist: LIGHT, LIGHTHOUSE.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The lighthouse study now wishes to dress the beam. In stripes.

papers.text: Flash your initials from a lighthouse. Then your name, all night.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: A study: is a humming kite an instrument? If so, it joins the band.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The kite study asks to hear a whistling kite, and one that sighs.

papers.text: A plaque on each lamp: LIT BY THE PRESIDENT. I have done four.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: Does the anglers' willow need permission to droop? A study.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The willow study asks to inspect every willow for drooping.

papers.text: Three small umbrellas, one per telephone. Bad lines are so damp.
papers.subject: vanity

favour.text: About the umbrellas: they wish to judge the marrow show. Open.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S UMBRELLA JUDGES MARROWS; GROWERS DAMP
clippings.refuse: UMBRELLAS STAY BY THE TELEPHONES, OPINIONS UNSHARED

papers.text: Kites land on awnings. A study finds 9 in 10 prefer stripes.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The awning study asks to try plain awnings too. And spots.

papers.text: Glaze the park's bean rows. Then price cards. Then a shop bell.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A study of the band's quietest tune. Of 40, the interval leads.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The tune study asks for a longer interval, to be thorough.

papers.text: Hedge the park's coach turning circle. Coaches will learn to turn square.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A study of the 900 park benches. 3 face a road. The rest, hedge.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The bench study needs a second sitting. Some benches were taken.

papers.text: Go window-shopping, for the camera. We have wrapped you a window.
papers.subject: vanity

papers.text: The hedge show wants the marrow show's day. Hedges do not wilt.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Open the coach stop cut into the park hedge. Stand in for the coach.
papers.subject: buses

papers.text: The anglers have had 211 still evenings. The band would like one.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Tour the provinces with the national pumpkin. Front seat. Wave second.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: The Mill's first ribbon. Uncut. It could open something? No reason.
papers.subject: ribbons

favour.text: About the ribbon: it would like to lead the Sunday concert.

clippings.sign: RIBBON LEADS BAND; BAND FOLLOWS, PUZZLED
clippings.refuse: RIBBON STAYS IN ITS BOX, UNCUT AND UNSURE

papers.text: Mow a kite runway by the coach stop. Ours have nowhere to taxi.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A sign on your fountain, paid for: COACHES, AWAY FROM SHOPS.
papers.subject: fountains

papers.text: A study: are the park's leek beds straight enough to be beds?
papers.subject: gardens
papers.biggerStudy: The bed study asks to inspect each leek row from a ladder.

papers.text: Every Mill ribbon to say CUT BY THE PRESIDENT. Before you cut it.
papers.subject: ribbons

papers.text: Cufflinks: two small fountains in your shape. A tie pin follows.
papers.subject: fountains

favour.text: About the cufflinks: they would like a seat at the Quiet Competition.

clippings.sign: PRESIDENT'S CUFFLINKS JOIN QUIET COMPETITION; TRICKLE
clippings.refuse: CUFFLINKS KEPT IN A DRAWER, STILL RUNNING

papers.text: The marrows have had the band's front row since the napkin. Move them.

papers.text: A study of the next Mill ribbon shade. 40 beiges so far, on the band.
papers.subject: committees
papers.biggerStudy: The shade study wants 40 more beiges. Two of the first matched.

papers.text: Unveil the national pumpkin's arcade plinth. Bow after it does.
papers.subject: vegetable-shows

papers.text: We will pay to judge your lawn's edges. Kites off it, pending.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A bandstand on the kite field. Its roof is a lovely place to land.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Lend us a corner of the hedge show lawn. Kites need very little. At first.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: A Mill window display: RIBBON, BEING MADE. Rosettes, round the back.
papers.subject: ribbons

papers.text: A fountain in your shape in each province. Rodney wants a tenth.
papers.subject: fountains

papers.text: Fly the motto on a kite: PROUDLY ADEQUATE. It flies about that well.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Move the spotters' bench. Our hedge now has a bench-shaped gap.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Your signature printed on every form. Then you need never read one.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: Cut the ribbon on our new notebook. Small scissors have been found.
papers.subject: ribbons

papers.text: We will pay for a still lake. Reflected kites must apply.

papers.text: A study of where the band stands. It is standing in the arcade.

papers.text: Mill ribbon tails for every kite: a metre, then two. Hedges get the rest.

papers.text: Keep time for the band's lake concert. Rodney will frame it.
papers.subject: bandstands

papers.text: Form 7 of the Republic is for coaches. The Guild keeps filing hats on it.
papers.subject: paperwork

papers.text: We will pay to keep the park hedges in shape. Ours: a hat.
papers.subject: hedges

papers.text: Feed the ducks at the Quiet Competition, for the camera. Mime the crumbs.
papers.subject: ducks

papers.text: We will hire the growers' bean canes at night. Kites sleep upright.
papers.subject: kites

papers.text: Swap the lake hedge for a bench. 3 fish in 4 ask who is there.
papers.subject: gardens

papers.text: A study of the kite form. Its one box says NO, in the Committee's hand.
papers.subject: paperwork
papers.biggerStudy: The study asks for a form to add a box. That form has no box either.

papers.text: Growers water from our lake: a can, a hose, a pump. It is one duck deep.

papers.text: Swap the park benches for hedge, clipped as benches. Rodney sat on one.

scripted.text: Welcome, President. I have welcomed three. I liked one.
scripted.subject: paperwork
scripted.note: the president's first paper: Mildred has seen three presidents and liked one, and never says which; teaches nothing new. Suggested effects as scripted-governor. Edited: punch moved to the last words; tagged statistic so the six scripted papers do not end on three undercuts.
